question: Can one global circular hue rotation plus one bounded 1D gamut-fraction map retain AO6 style without 3D covariance compression or an infeasible target?

operator.basis: deterministic orthonormal basis of the Rec.709 zero-luminance plane
operator.hue: one unweighted circular Procrustes rotation between valid CB11 and AO6 unit chroma directions
operator.gamut_fraction: chroma magnitude divided by exact maximum magnitude on the fixed-luminance RGB cube section
operator.fraction_fit: one ordinary least-squares affine from CB11 to AO6 clipped-logit gamut fraction
operator.reconstruction: rotated CB11 hue and sigmoid-predicted gamut fraction at exact CB11 luminance
operator.neutral_rule: CB11 chroma below 1e-12 remains exact neutral
operator.scale: unchanged analytical safe step only for source-boundary and float32 margin preservation
operator.forbidden: 3D covariance, local hue/fraction, robust weights, nonlinear fraction curve, slope clipping, target dose, semantic mask or post-score rescue

research_basis.modflows: AAAI 2025 / arXiv:2503.19062 invertible RGB transport comparator
research_basis.position: clean-room two-factor bounded baseline; no paper code, model, weights or novelty claim

stop_rules: Any hue/fraction fit, envelope or automatic failure closes before visual preference.
Any severe or preference failure closes without changing coordinates, fit or slope envelope.
Pass opens only a wholly new source confirmation.
claim_ceiling: Development-only bounded circular hue/fraction transport evidence on consumed CC0 display proxies; not fresh confirmation, stock response, calibration, population preference or product promotion.
